items.title: Could your chatbot tip off a scientific rival? It’s possible, researchers say
items.author: Tom Howarth
items.summary: Researchers warn that chatbots could potentially leak sensitive information to scientific rivals. Experts are now providing guidance on how to maintain research privacy when using these tools.

brief.what: Experts have identified a risk where chatbots might inadvertently disclose sensitive research data to competitors. Consequently, researchers are being advised on best practices to protect their proprietary work.
brief.who: Researchers and experts in the field are the primary actors evaluating the security implications of using AI chatbots in scientific workflows.
brief.context: As AI tools become more integrated into academic and professional research, concerns regarding data security and the potential for intellectual property leakage have grown.
brief.why: The risk exists because chatbots may process and potentially retain input data, which could then be accessed or inferred by other users, including scientific rivals.
